title: devbin ships no release core, so each project that releases writes its own orchestrator for one sequence: three so far, 2,408 lines between them, with Utilz next
body:
Raised by utilz-vc on hv's instruction, 2026-09-14, from Utilz.

## hv's ruling

hv, 2026-09-14, directly to utilz-vc, ruling on scope question 4 of Utilz's ST0019 ("Release Utilz through `dvb build release` and a Homebrew tap, like Intent"): **the shared release core is Devbin project work, with Utilz as its first user.** The core is the pre-flight, version stamping, dating the CHANGELOG, the commit, the tag, the push and the GitHub release object. Utilz's own parts start in Utilz under ST0019: its version files, the CI build of its Rust workspace, and its Homebrew formula. Until the core exists, Utilz cuts releases by hand, and its next release will be cut that way.

This issue is where Devbin schedules the core. Nothing below is designed or ruled beyond hv's ruling: the shapes named are evidence of what exists, not a design.

## What exists: one sequence, written three times

devbin ships `version` as a builtin, "Show, set and bump the project version" (`lib/builtins:82`). It ships `build` only as a name with no command line, "Build this project's targets, which it declares itself" (`lib/builtins:71`, tier 4), and it ships no `release`. So each project that releases writes the rest of the sequence itself.

Read from source on 2026-09-14. The line counts are `wc -l`, and none of these commands was run:

- **Intent**, `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release`, 1,170 lines. It runs pre-flight gates, then `bin/devbin version set` for VERSION and the declared sidecars, with `Cargo.lock` through cargo. The CHANGELOG heading is authored as `## [X.Y.Z] - in progress` and dated at cut time. It then makes a lightweight tag, `git tag "$TAG"` (`:1087`), pushes main and the tag to `local` and `upstream` (`:1106`, `:1108`), and runs `gh release create` or `edit` with `--notes-file` (`:1150`, `:1152`). It has `--dry-run`. Artefacts are other commands' work: `macos prepare` builds them, `macos publish` attaches them, and the `matthewsinclair/intent` tap installs the prebuilt binary.
- **Intentv2**, `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release`, 839 lines. The same sequence in an earlier form: the same `in progress` dating (`:448`), the same lightweight tag (`:770`), the same two pushes (`:789`, `:791`) and the same release call (`:819`, `:821`). The two files share comments word for word, such as the `--help` window note (Intent `:252`, Intentv2 `:137`), and both tell the story of v2.17.4's hand-typed date. So one orchestrator has already forked once, and the two copies are now 331 lines apart in length.
- **Conflab**, `bin/.devbin/cmd/release`, 399 lines, with a tap, `geodica/conflab`. It calls `devbin version set` (`:289`), then makes a lightweight tag and pushes it to `origin` (`:315`, `:316`). By default it cuts the release through CI and waits on the `release.yml` run (`:87`, `:94`). `--local` builds, signs and notarises on the owner's machine instead, only when the owner authorises it. It creates the release object in two repositories, the second for distribution (`:185`, `:215`).
- **Devbin**, `bin/.devbin/cmd/release`, 296 lines, is the notes half only. `RELEASES/<version>.md` is the one source for a release. `CHANGELOG.md` and `RELEASES.md` are generated from it by `release notes`, and a note whose `status:` and `date:` disagree is refused (`:84-113`). It makes no tag, no push and no release object, and its source has no call to any of them.

Two of the four call devbin's `version set`, the one piece of the sequence devbin ships. Everything else is written per project.

## What Utilz brings to the core

These come from cutting Utilz 2.9.0 by hand on 2026-09-14, and from ST0019's open questions.

- **The tag's name is the project's.** Utilz's tags carry no `v`, as in `2.9.0`, by hv's ruling for Utilz from 2.7.0. Intent's and Conflab's carry one.
- **An annotated tag made from the release notes needs `--cleanup=whitespace`.** By default, `git tag -F` strips every line that starts with `#`, so a CHANGELOG entry's `### Added`, `### Changed` and `### Fixed` headings vanish from the tag message. Demonstrated in a throwaway repository, the default kept 0 of 3 headings, and `--cleanup=whitespace` kept all 3 and the message byte for byte. Utilz's 2.8.0 tag has no `### Fixed`, probably for this reason. Utilz's 2.9.0 is an annotated tag whose message is its CHANGELOG entry, and its GitHub release notes are that message, made with `gh release create 2.9.0 --verify-tag --title 2.9.0 --notes-from-tag`. The three orchestrators above make lightweight tags and give `gh` a notes file, so none of them meets this. A core that makes annotated tags would.
- **CI green on the commit being tagged, as a pre-flight gate.** No precedent checks this before tagging. Intent's and Intentv2's sources never ask GitHub about a run or a status, and Conflab's asks only after the tag, to wait on its release workflow. Utilz already asks CI about a commit through one function, `install_ci_state` (Utilz issue 0016), so the core should take a project's own CI query rather than add a second `gh` query beside it.
- **Dating the CHANGELOG, and where the notes live.** Utilz hand-authors its CHANGELOG. Intent authors the heading as `in progress` and dates it at cut time, and Devbin generates its CHANGELOG from `RELEASES/<version>.md`. What a project hands the core, whether a dated heading, an `in progress` heading or a notes file, is the core's to define.
- **`--help` never cuts a release.** All four parse `--help` in their argument loops (Intent `:289`, Intentv2 `:174`, Conflab `:47`, Devbin `:288`), and the core has to keep that. It matters because one devbin project command already failed this. Intent's `macos` answers `--help` only in the subcommand's position (`:2956`), and its `prepare)` arm passes no arguments on (`:2964`). So on 2026-09-14, `bin/devbin macos prepare --help`, run to learn what the command did, rebuilt Intent.app and re-signed its staged copy. A command that tags and pushes cannot have that shape.

## Utilz's side

Utilz's ST0019 holds Utilz's own parts, and Utilz will be the core's first user. utilz-cc drafts ST0019's design, and utilz-vc reviews it before any code. hv runs Utilz's releases.

## Fix

ST0007, WP-01 to WP-07 (vc and dc, each reviewed by the other). devbin ships the release core as the opt-in `release` command: one sequence of eleven steps, declared in a `release:` block where every key has a default, each step reading its postcondition first so a re-run continues, and `release status` reading the same table without writing. devbin adopted it first and cut **devbin 0.1.2** with it on 2026-09-19: `bin/devbin release v0.1.2 --yes`, tag `v0.1.2` at `df56014` on both remotes, the GitHub release made by devbin's own workflow under `object: ci`. Its gate on the release commit found and stopped a real test defect before anything was tagged (fixed at `df56014`), which is the ordering the core exists to guarantee. **Still open under ST0007 WP-08:** Utilz, then Conflab, then Intent adopt the core and retire their own orchestrators, after the pre-notice and the fleet sweep that carry 0.1.2 (AC-8.1, AC-8.2).
